prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a landscape 3:2 Minecraft builder reference sheet, crisp voxel style, vanilla Minecraft blocks only, plain light background, no characters or animals. Two views side by side: LEFT a straight-on front elevation, orthographic; RIGHT an elevated three-quarter view at the same scale that reveals the east passage and rear garden. Show the same complete build in both views. Skilled human builder quality: real massing and depth, projecting pilasters and cornices, recessed framed openings, real roof verges, eaves and ridge, stairs, slabs, fences, walls, trapdoors and lanterns. Keep all geometry on a believable Minecraft block grid.
Site: A narrow, handsome red-brick shop house standing alone on its plot in a shopping street, its steep dark-slate gable facing the road. At pavement level a tall open shopfront nine blocks wide sits between two dark-oak pilasters. Behind the counters, butcher's goods show as pink_terracotta pork chops, brown_mushroom_block baked chicken and red_terracotta steaks, all block-built. Over the shopfront runs a deep maroon red_nether_bricks fascia lettered exactly BUTCHER in white_banner/white_wall_banner white lettering, with a red_wool and white_wool striped awning hanging from it. A dark_oak_hanging_sign juts from the right-hand pilaster. To the left is a smaller bay with the family's own dark_oak_door double door, a glass_pane fanlight and a little dark-oak timber hood with a lantern at each end. Above, a crisp smooth_quartz cornice carries two storeys of bricks with three paired sash windows per floor, set back into the wall under white smooth_quartz lintels, with dark_oak_trapdoor shutters on the top floor. White smooth_quartz quoins climb the corners. The gable has a small loft window and dark-oak verges with a deepslate slate ridge, and a dormer pokes from each side slope. A tall brick chimney with a deepslate_bricks dark band and smoking campfire cap rises up the east side beside a gravel passage that leads to a spruce_fence_gate garden gate with a spruce_fence lamp post and lantern. Behind, a lower two-storey brick back wing runs off the west half under its own slate gable, with a smoking kitchen chimney on its end. The rest of the back is a spruce-fenced kitchen garden: farmland beds of carrots, potatoes, beetroots and wheat with water channels, dirt_path paths from the kitchen door and the shop's back door, composter compost bins, a water_cauldron water butt, a spruce_stairs/spruce_slab bench and an oak_log/oak_leaves apple tree in the far corner. Use oak_leaves to suggest the apple tree without adding non-vanilla fruit blocks.
Size: plot 28 blocks wide, 39 deep; house 16 x 18 with an 8 x 9 rear wing; 3 storeys (shop + 2 home floors) plus gable loft; ridge about 33 blocks high. Preserve the narrow tall proportions and distinctly lower rear wing.

Additional permitted functional/decor ids: lantern, ladder, campfire, barrel, cauldron, water_cauldron, iron_chain, white_banner, white_wall_banner, dark_oak_hanging_sign, dark_oak_wall_sign, flower_pot, composter.

changes: Saved the unmodified generated image as concept.png in the current directory.

The role lists retain every planned block, including blocks not visible in the image. Visible material ids are interpretations of raster concept art, not a verified Minecraft block inventory; flower species, crop varieties and some timber or stone variants cannot be determined exactly.
The left elevation shows slight top-surface visibility at the pavement and projecting details, rather than a strictly orthographic projection.
Exact plot dimensions, house and wing footprints, nine-block shop opening and 33-block ridge height are not demonstrated by a measurable block grid.
Each home floor has three individual sash-style windows rather than three clearly paired window assemblies.
The loft window is much larger than a small loft opening and has added shutters.
White window mullions and thin frames use shapes that glass_pane and the specified quartz blocks cannot reproduce at the depicted scale.
Added flower boxes under all three lower home-floor windows, small shop plants, and lanterns visible inside the home windows. White flowers are approximated as oxeye_daisy in the palette.
The BUTCHER lettering is rendered as raised solid white characters rather than visibly constructed banner lettering.
The hanging sign adds a white meat-cleaver emblem and a thin metal bracket whose exact shape is not reproducible with the specified blocks.
Added hanging meat displays behind the counter. Their curved silhouettes, hooks and small cuts are not literal vanilla block geometry.
Counter goods are miniature pink, tan and red chunks rather than full block-sized terracotta and mushroom blocks; the brown goods appear considerably lighter than brown_mushroom_block.
The awning has thin fabric-like edges and sloping surfaces rather than fully block-thick wool construction.
The front door fanlight contains ornate thin latticework beyond ordinary glass_pane geometry, and the timber hood has a more elaborate stepped pediment.
Dormers are represented in both side slopes by the elevation, but only the east dormer is clearly visible in the three-quarter view.
The rear wing appears substantially exposed to the east in the three-quarter view; its required placement off the west half and exact two-storey height cannot be confirmed.

The east gravel passage opens through a broad wooden gate near the front of the garden, rather than clearly terminating at a rear garden gate. Its lamp post has a dark slender support rather than an unambiguous spruce_fence post.
Gravel is the dominant garden access surface; separate dirt_path routes from both the kitchen and shop back doors are not clearly shown.
Added a subdividing garden fence, substantial oak-leaf hedges, timber-edged beds and extra barrels.
The tree contains no identifiable apples. All four requested crop varieties are suggested, but potatoes cannot be distinguished reliably from the other green crops.
The back wing and main house obscure rear doors and part of the garden; a distinct shop back door is not visible.
The pavement resembles stone_bricks and stone_brick_slab in addition to the planned street palette, and dark chimney caps suggest deepslate_brick_slab.
Smoking chimney caps show exposed flames; the planned hay_block smoke boosters are not visible.
The two views differ slightly in shop interior arrangement and fine facade details, so they are not perfectly consistent projections of one block model.
